slides.say: A circle with center O has a radius of four centimeters. The opposite sides A D and B C of rectangle A B C D are tangent to the circle at E and F. The area of the rectangle equals the area of the circle. What is the length of B C?

We'll solve it two ways, with a short equation, and then with an estimate, a size check on the choices. [short pause] The equation first. A D touches the circle at E, and B C touches it at F. Remember, the radius to the point where a tangent touches the circle is perpendicular to the tangent.

So O E and O F are both perpendicular to the two parallel sides, and together they make one straight line from E to F. That's a diameter, two times four, eight. And it's as long as the side A B, so the height of the rectangle is eight.

The area of the rectangle is A B times B C, so it's eight times B C. The area of the circle is pi r squared, pi times four squared, sixteen pi. The two areas are equal, so eight times B C is sixteen pi.

so eight times B C is sixteen pi

slides.say: To get B C alone, we divide both sides by eight. Sixteen pi over eight is two pi. Choice number two is our answer. The math solution wasn't bad at all.

Choice number two is our answer

slides.say: [pause] Now the same question with an estimate, a size check, and almost no calculation. Draw the square around the circle. Its side is the diameter, eight, so its area is eight times eight, sixty-four.

The circle is inside this square, so the circle's area is less than sixty-four. The rectangle has the same area as the circle, so eight times B C is also less than sixty-four. That means B C is less than eight.

That means B C is less
